title: Hot spots conjecture for simply-connected planar and convex domains
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a simply-connected planar domain, or a convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $u$ be a second Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian on $\Omega$.

**Hot spots conjecture.** The function $u$ attains its maximum only on the boundary $\partial\Omega$. The source presents this as the restricted formulation motivated by counterexamples to the original conjecture. The paper establishes the relevant triangle case, while the full assertion for all simply-connected planar domains and all convex domains in every dimension is not resolved in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12659

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2023). “Based on these counterexamples, the hot spots conjecture now is stated as follows.”
source_name: Hongbin Chen, Changfeng Gui and Ruofei Yao, “Uniqueness of critical points of the second Neumann eigenfunctions on triangles”, arXiv:2311.12659 (2025).

solutions.summary: Claimed by OpenAI. Claims strict hot spots for smooth bounded simply connected planar domains, including multiple first positive Neumann eigenvalues: every corresponding nonzero eigenfunction has no interior critical point and all extrema lie on the boundary.
solutions.body:
Claimed by OpenAI. Claims strict hot spots for smooth bounded simply connected planar domains, including multiple first positive Neumann eigenvalues: every corresponding nonzero eigenfunction has no interior critical point and all extrema lie on the boundary.

Scope relative to this problem: This addresses the smooth bounded simply connected planar branch of the target. It keeps every corresponding nonzero first-positive Neumann eigenfunction, including eigenvalue multiplicity, with no interior critical points and boundary extrema. It does not establish the arbitrary-dimensional convex-domain branch or mixed-boundary and quantum-graph hot-spots assertions.
